nodes.label: CHANGELOG.md
nodes.rationale: The project's changelog: 152 version entries from 1.0.0 to 1.78.2, each written as prose recording the decision taken and the bug that prompted it rather than a bullet of the diff. Every 'found and fixed' entry has a test pinning it, which is what makes the list trustworthy; it is the most-read file after the README and the record of why each standing constraint in CLAUDE.md exists.

nodes.label: 1.78.2 — A test that held the migration's overlap has nothing left to overlap
nodes.rationale: test_routes_move_one_at_a_time grepped index.js for the in-function and remote route sets and held that they did not intersect; since 1.78.0 removed callCalculator the remote set was empty and both checks passed vacuously, one under the name 'the calculator still answers what has not moved, until it goes'. A check that cannot fail reads as evidence and is not, so the two checks and a per-resolver grep for the same identifier are removed; the scope block's file-wide 'nothing in the resolver reaches a remote' already holds the absence. What remains is the inventory: every route index.js answers is in IN_FUNCTION_ROUTES and every inventoried route is one routes.py declares. Found by a knowledge-graph trace of what still depended on the retired service.

nodes.label: 1.78.1 — The hosted service's own files go
nodes.rationale: 1.78.0 stopped calling the calculator; this deletes it: service/app.py with its socket and two auth verifiers, the Dockerfile, requirements.txt, the smoke test and scan gate, the provisioning script, the CI container job and pip steps, and make serve-calc. service/ is routes.py and a README; tests/test_service.py keeps its name so nothing pointing at it moves and asserts exactly that, with call() answering through routes.answer so the projection and refusal checks did not change. The tests of the retired thing (auth seam, token verifier, Dockerfile reconstruction, startup guard, Debian update line) went with it, and the docs keep retired sections marked rather than rewritten as the record of what was built.

nodes.label: 1.78.0 — The remote is gone, and with it the calculator: every figure is computed inside the Forge function
nodes.rationale: Last commit of the series ADR 0031 ordered: with burndown moved in 1.77.5 nothing named the calculator, so the remotes block and its three Cloud Run hostnames leave the manifest, invokeRemote and callCalculator leave the resolver, and deploy.yml is deleted. Removing a remote declaring realms and operations:[compute] proved a major version (the second probe had said minor): 8.9.0 became 9.0.0 with forge install --upgrade, and the app is now eligible for Runs on Atlassian. 9.0.0 shipped for eleven minutes having deleted answerHere by accident, because esbuild bundles an undefined identifier silently; 9.1.0 restored it and the suite gained a guard that every bare call in the resolver names something defined, imported or runtime-provided. tests/test_service.py inverts its remote assertions (no remotes block, no egress, no invokeRemote, no .run.app under forge/); ADR 0012 and ADR 0030 are superseded; the Google Cloud resources still to delete are listed with commands.

nodes.label: 1.77.5 — The burndown is answered inside the Forge function, and nothing reaches the calculator any more
nodes.rationale: The last route to move under ADR 0031: /v1/burndown is one sprint's daily series, and the context resolver's one call now goes to answerHere. Every figure a tenant sees is computed by the Python inside the function; callCalculator has no caller left but stays one more commit with the remotes block and invokeRemote import, because retiring a remote is its own change to blame. Deployed to development as 8.9.0, a minor version.

nodes.label: 1.77.4 — The trend series is answered inside the Forge function
nodes.rationale: The fifth route to move under ADR 0031, a plain call: /v1/history is one row per sprint, and the context resolver's two calls (the series and the re-read after a recordable row is stored) go to answerHere. Only the identifier changed at two sites; the inventory in tests/test_service.py gains the route. burndown remains on the calculator. Deployed as 8.8.0.

nodes.label: 1.77.3 — The forecast is a job, because the forecast on a real board does not fit a resolver call
nodes.rationale: 1.77.2's synchronous in-function forecast failed on the dev site when the adapter's fifteen seconds ran out: the forecast alone took 12 to 15 seconds because the board has 906 mostly-zero working-day observations and 31 open items, so forecast_completion walks about 280 days per trial across 20,000 trials. ADR 0031's 'facts and the forecast stay synchronous' was wrong for a long sparse history and carries a dated correction. The sequencing machinery is generalised: startJob is the one function both resolvers call, simulationConsumer on simulation-fn drains the simulations queue running whichever allow-listed route the event names, and jobResult (replacing sequenceResult) finishes a forecast by re-reading at-risk titles and assignees from Jira by key and writing the calibration log. A forecast's payload exceeds the 100 KB event limit, so the projection travels through app storage in 160 KB chunks capped at 4 MB. tests/jobs_shapes.mjs and tests/test_service.py hold the forecast kind, the chunk round trip, the guard order and the adapter on both routes. nodejs24.x and 1,024 MB kept. Deployed as 8.7.0.

nodes.label: 1.77.2 — The forecast is answered inside the Forge function
nodes.rationale: The third route to move under ADR 0031 and the one a reader clicks: /v1/slice and /v1/forecast-context move together because a slice chosen in-function and a forecast computed remotely would be two runtimes agreeing about a list, which nothing checks. The brief's forecast call moved with it. Measured on the second probe: 1.5 s warm at 480 issues, 2.8 s at 4,800, about 6 s cold. Only the identifier changed at three sites; the inventory in tests/test_service.py gains both routes. history and burndown remain. Deployed as 8.3.0.

nodes.label: 1.77.1 — The facts route is answered inside the Forge function
nodes.rationale: The second route to move under ADR 0031 and the first that keeps its shape: /v1/facts answers in a third of a second warm, so it moves as a call. answerHere(path, body) is callCalculator's drop-in with the same routes, bodies, envelope and {available: false, sentence} refusal, backed by runtime.answer from the memory snapshot. Both callers changed: the facts resolver and the scheduled brief's boardFigures, so weekly-brief-fn now declares 1,024 MB too. tests/test_service.py holds an inventory of moved routes: the answerHere set equals it, is disjoint from the callCalculator set, and both are routes routes.py declares. Deployed as 8.2.0.

nodes.label: 1.77.0 — Sequencing runs inside the Forge function, as a job, and the page cannot tell
nodes.rationale: The first route to move under ADR 0031, and the one that had to change shape: sequencing is cubic and twelve asks is three and a half minutes on Forge's CPU. The sequence resolver validates via /v1/sequence-check (the same check_sequence, run in-function from the memory snapshot), refuses payloads over the 100 KB event limit, pushes to the sequence-jobs queue, writes a job row bound to the asking account and answers 202. A sequence-fn consumer (900 s, 1,024 MB) reads Forge's retry context before loading anything and refuses on any retry, loads the runtime plain (a snapshot load runs 1.65x slower), runs /v1/sequence and writes a result row. sequenceResult collects with 202, the answer with titles and bases joined back, a refusal, or 404/403/410, deleting rows on hand-over; an in-flight key hashed from context, projection and account makes a reload join the running job. Polling lives in forge/bridge/bridge.js; src/app.js is untouched. The event carries ids only, titles stay in the job row, and three stores are declared in ADR 0018's inventory. forge/src/jobs.js is the pure half, run by tests/jobs_shapes.mjs over twelve rows held by tests/test_service.py alongside the manifest-versus-code queue name, guard order and adapter back-off. Deployed as 8.1.0, minor; still ineligible for Runs on Atlassian while the remotes block stands.

nodes.label: 1.76.2 — A sixth suite: the same Python under WebAssembly, byte for byte
nodes.rationale: tests/test_wasm.py succeeds the hosted service's parity test: it regenerates forge/src/assets.js with the deploy generator, answers every route the service suite exercises natively through routes.answer with sorted keys, answers the same bodies through forge/src/runtime.js in one Node process per load mode (snapshot and plain), and compares the strings. Fourteen cases match; the snapshot loads in 170 ms against 1.1 s plain. It asserts every .py in agent/tools/ is in the bundle. make test-wasm runs it, make test includes it, CI runs it under Node 24. The loader now removes earlier bundles' directories because the snapshot makes every digest new and /tmp is 512 MB.

nodes.label: 1.76.1 — The Python runtime travels into the Forge function as a generated module, and the loader that unpacks it exists
nodes.rationale: make forge-assets runs forge/build-assets.mjs: it reads the pinned pyodide 314.0.6 package, every .py in agent/tools/ and service/routes.py, writes them gzip-and-base64 into the git-ignored forge/src/assets.js, and adds a memory snapshot taken after the sources are imported (16 MB, one second). The file is git-ignored and the security suite asserts it, because a second copy of the Python drifts (ADR 0031). forge/src/runtime.js unpacks once per container keyed by digest, imports Pyodide through a Function the bundler cannot rewrite, loads from the snapshot or plain, and answer(path, body) hands the route to routes.answer. The boot sequence is one exported string shared by loader and generator. Nothing in the resolver calls it yet.

nodes.label: 1.76.0 — The calculator's answers are one module, and the socket in front of them is another
nodes.rationale: First code change under ADR 0031: service/app.py held the projection, caps, refusals and eight route functions (what a Forge function must run under WebAssembly) together with HTTP, two auth verifiers and the body limit (which stay with the hosted service). The first half is now service/routes.py ending in answer(path, body); app.py imports and re-exports it and adds nothing to any envelope, held literally by a test that handle() and answer() return the same bytes and that routes.py imports nothing WebAssembly lacks. Sequencing is capped at twelve asks in the tool: intake.MAX_ASKS and intake.too_many_asks() consulted by intake.sequence() so the file transport refuses identically; route_sequence splits into check_sequence (refuses everything, computes nothing) and the route, so the resolver can check before starting a job. tests pin thirteen asks refused instantly and the 413 carrying the tool's sentence.

nodes.label: 1.75.1 — ADR 0031 priced sequencing per ask, and the cost is cubic
nodes.rationale: A second throwaway Forge app measured sequencing of 4, 8, 12 and 16 asks at 1.1, 7, 21 and 48 seconds natively and ten times that on Forge, so the fifty-ask cap described a computation of about twenty-five minutes nobody had run. ADR 0031 now caps sequencing at twelve on every transport, declares the consumer at 900 seconds, drops the first-ask timing guard and keeps the retry guard (a killed consumer is retried after forty seconds). The memory snapshot (1.3 s cold against 11 s, 1.65x slower compute) goes on the resolver function, not the consumer. A reload mid-job joins the running job. The probe settled by deploy that a consumer module is minor, adding a remote major, removing one minor (the last later contradicted by 1.78.0). Measurements in docs/research/2026-09-02-second-probe-consumer-and-snapshot.md; no code changed.

nodes.label: 1.75.0 — The app will run its forecast inside the Forge function, and the calculator will be retired
nodes.rationale: 1.74.3 corrected ADR 0008 to say a WebAssembly route existed and left the choice open; ADR 0031 makes it: the existing Python under Pyodide inside the function, one implementation of every figure, no remote, no egress, and the Runs on Atlassian badge earned when the remotes block leaves. The record carries the design reached in three rounds: sequencing becomes an async event polled by the adapter so the page and ADR 0009 stay untouched, the consumer's budget and two guards, where a result waits and who may collect it, how the runtime travels, and the order routes move with the calculator answering until each has moved; rejected shapes are recorded. Nothing in code changed; research in docs/research/2026-09-01-forge-async-events.md; ADR 0012 and ADR 0030 stay true until the remote goes; CONTEXT.md gains its first entry for calculator.

nodes.label: 1.74.4 — The manifest's badge comment no longer says there is no engineering answer
nodes.rationale: 1.74.3 left the comment stale because a manifest edit is a calculator redeploy and an app-id splice; this is that edit and nothing else moves. The comment now says what ADR 0008's amendment says: egress is the price of one implementation over a remote, a WebAssembly route inside the function exists and was measured, and the badge stays forfeit as a decision rather than a discovery.

nodes.label: 1.74.3 — ADR 0008 said the badge or a second forecast, with nothing in between; there is something in between, measured and recorded
nodes.rationale: ADR 0008 carries a dated amendment: the existing Python in agent/tools/ runs unchanged under Pyodide inside the Forge function with no remote, no egress and byte-identical figures, established on a throwaway Forge app on 2026-09-01 (docs/research/2026-09-01-runs-on-atlassian-badge.md) rather than from documentation, because the previous claim was written from documentation and was wrong. The decision is unchanged (the hosted calculator stands) but the trade is corrected: the badge plus retiring a pager-carrying service, against a forecast about ten times slower, a seven-second cold start, and sequencing at 13.6 s warm and 21 s cold for four asks. Removing a remote is recorded as minor (later found wrong) and a no-remote app is PINNED for residency. The manifest comment is left stale for the next manifest change.

nodes.label: 1.74.2 — The guard added in 1.74.0 did not run on the change it exists for
nodes.rationale: The realm guard lives in the deploy workflow, which triggers on service/**, agent/tools/** and itself; the manifest is none of those, so 1.74.1's declaration of GB, the one manifest change that most needed checking, was the one the check sat out. Had the URL been a typo a UK tenant would have been routed at an unverified hostname for up to a week. forge/manifest.yml is now a trigger path, commented as being there for the guard and not the image.

nodes.label: 1.74.1 — GB is declared, and a UK tenant's numbers are now computed in London
nodes.rationale: The realm points at the europe-west2 service 1.74.0 deployed, declared only after it existed because a realm naming a URL that does not answer is the stale-calculator failure from the other end (ADR 0030). Atlassian's EU realm is Frankfurt and Dublin; the UK is a separate realm, and what Forge does with an undeclared realm is documented nowhere (a refused install or a silent fall-through to the US). Pointing GB at Frankfurt was rejected as falsifying the claim that the app never gets the region wrong. forge lint priced it as a major version ('data residency or egress modification'), free while the only installation is the dev site.

nodes.label: 1.74.0 — A third Cloud Run region, London, and a check that makes the drift it invites impossible
nodes.rationale: ADR 0030 decided GB gets its own service; europe-west2 is deployed here and declared in the next change. deploy.yml hardcoded two region names twice; REGIONS is set once and both the loop and the summary read it, because a service that exists and quietly stops receiving versions is the worst failure class. A new step reads the realms out of forge/manifest.yml and fails the run on a declared realm with no deployment, warning only on an undeclared deployed region; proved over three states before CI. A per-region preflight prints the gcloud registry-create command rather than widening the deploy identity beyond artifactregistry.writer. service/provision-gcp.sh carries three regions.

nodes.label: 1.73.0 — Two entries in forge/manifest.yml were free to change until the first external install, and both are now decided
nodes.rationale: ADR 0030 records them together. The calculator keeps its *.run.app hostnames permanently: the argument that a custom domain is the only indirection between manifest and infrastructure collapsed on Google's documentation that a project migrated into an organisation keeps its ids and URLs, and Cloud Run's domain mappings are preview and unsupported in europe-west3. GB is declared with its own London service because the UK is not inside EU; pointing it at Frankfurt was rejected as a quiet lie. forge lint accepts GB and rejects ZZ with MANIFEST_INVALID_RULE, and prices the change as major. What an undeclared realm does to a tenant is documented nowhere and decides whether DE and CH follow. A third region is a deploy.yml change, never a hand deployment. CLAUDE.md's table gained ADR 0028, 0029 and 0030; the hosting doc's open questions are answered in place and dated.

nodes.label: 1.72.4 — The roadmap named one piece of engineering between here and a Marketplace listing, and it had been built the day before
nodes.rationale: docs/roadmap.md said sequencing needed a way to read an ask out of Jira; item 7 closed on 2026-08-31 in four slices and the file referenced neither ADR 0028 nor 0029. Three places now say the engineering list is empty. One claim was wrong when written: the needed-by date has always been dueDate and asks_from_issues() reads it; the real gaps are a problem statement and a success measure, which readiness names. CONTEXT.md still defined an ask by the absence of tickets; Ask is redefined per ADR 0028, Candidate added, Band added as the reference-class selector ADR 0029 argues, Reference class amended; both new entries were checked against asks_from_issues() and candidate_issues() rather than the records, which corrected two of them.

nodes.label: 1.72.3 — Two runbooks opened by telling the reader the calculator was not deployed, and it has been since the afternoon they were written
nodes.rationale: docs/hosting-the-calculator.md and docs/forge-deployment.md carried openings true on 2026-08-25 and false by that afternoon. A stale opening is read and believed before anything that contradicts it, and it propagated: a session handoff stated the calculator was unprovisioned, CLAUDE.md said the same until 1.72.0, and forge/src/jira.js hardcoded an empty burndown for several versions on its strength. The framing is dated rather than deleted, with observations recorded beside the estimates they confirm; drifted claims about the baseUrl, forge lint, operations: [compute], the invocation-token headers, the container and the scanner are closed. No behaviour changed; the control is that a claim about what exists carries its date.

nodes.label: 1.72.2 — A sprint whose whole window is still ahead of it was told its dataset was too old
nodes.rationale: MOBL Sprint 4 (window 11-25 September, completed 31 August) has every burndown day in the future and every row null, and the page's one explanation, that the dataset predated the item/point toggle and needed re-import, was false. noDaysYetNote() now decides from the entry's own dates before the calculator is called: a sprint in the future has not started, and a closed sprint whose completion precedes its start is a Jira data problem worth naming, pointing at the same dates that decided its value crediting in 1.71.0. Mirrored in serve_live.py over one shared set of cases, proved by making the resolver's copy return null and watching the two disagree.

nodes.label: 1.72.1 — The burndown shipped broken and the tile said so
nodes.rationale: orgconfig.working_days returns date objects where the fetcher helper it replaced returned ISO strings, so the moved metrics.burndown threw comparing date to str on the derive branch; working_days_iso is what was wanted. The test passed because every dataset in the repository carries meta.workingDays, so the branch had no fixture, while a Forge resolver sends no working-day list and that is the only branch it takes: a test passing over the path nobody uses. The test now runs both branches and asserts byte-identical rows. The refusal reached the tile verbatim, which is why one screenshot found it; its punctuation is fixed.

nodes.label: 1.72.0 — The burndown tile has been blank on every Forge install since the bridge existed, and the sentence under it blamed the tenant's data
nodes.rationale: contextBody hardcoded burndown: [] because build_burndown lived in the fetcher and Forge cannot run Python; the calculator being provisioned changed that. The algorithm existed three times (fetcher, src/import.js, scripts/rebuild_burndown.py), so metrics.burndown became the one implementation the calculator serves and build_burndown a two-line delegate, verified byte-identical against the real board. /v1/burndown follows /v1/history; the service validates, delegates and passes rows back, held byte for byte. A period with no clock is refused; meta.workingDays stays the caller's (ADR 0011). burndownNote travels always, null when nothing to explain, naming which of four causes an empty chart has; WINDOW_HAS_NO_BURNDOWN in serve_live.py and the resolver's window branch are held equal (ADR 0009). The calculator deploys by pushing service/** or agent/tools/** to main, not forge deploy; CLAUDE.md corrected.

nodes.label: 1.71.0 — A tile said the wrong thing about a board where it was working correctly, and a refusal disproved itself in its own sentence
nodes.rationale: MOBL Sprint 4's Business Value tile blamed a below-level story while three finished epics worth $245,000 were silently excluded by a date window the sprint's own dates could not contain; ADR 0026's rule is unchanged, the exclusion was silent. creditableEpics() in forge/src/jira.js now returns what it credited and what it kept out, the context body carries valueWindow (Forge's alone, named in the parity check), and test_an_epic_the_window_excludes_is_counted_not_dropped pins it over the real dates. The sequencing tile refused with '11 observations, 10 needed': one `or` reported the item pair whichever of the two thresholds failed, at four sites in forecast.py. Each is two conditions with two sentences, Refusal carries its unit, tests/brief_shapes.mjs holds the strings, and the invariant that have is short of need is asserted.

nodes.label: 1.70.0 — A key a producer emits and no consumer takes is now a failing test
nodes.rationale: Three silent drops shipped in one session with every suite green: orgConfigOf named four keys and dropped the rest, the Forge sequence body lacked asks_considered, and contextBody carried setup while loadContext assigned nothing from it. A guard now runs both directions: every top-level key of a resolver body must be taken off the response by the consuming function, and every key the sequencing tile reads must be added by both transports or named one-sided (setup is Forge's alone). It reads the success body specifically, and tests/forge_shapes.mjs now passes a setup. What it cannot catch (a third branch, a taken-then-ignored key) is written in the test; tests/e2e.py compares the merged orgConfig against orgconfig.merge.

nodes.label: 1.69.1 — The value tile stops guessing
nodes.rationale: One sentence covered a field on no screen and a field not on the site, and was printed over a file too. Three states, each stated only when true, answered by /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/editmeta with no new scope and asked only when it would change what a reader is told. contextBody's setup key reached nobody (the third silent drop this session) and is kept on the context so switching boards cannot leave a stale diagnosis. A test_service guard pinned the literal 'the app cannot do that for them' and now tests the property: a tile that sends somebody to an administrator says why the app did not do it.

nodes.label: 1.69.0 — A t-shirt band declares candidacy, and the app stops guessing what a board still needs
nodes.rationale: Four text fields on four screens before anything worked was what an evaluation met first. A band now puts an epic forward on its own, an amendment reversing ADR 0028's refusal to infer, made safe by No, N and False so it is reversible out loud. candidate_answer has four answers with None for silence; the first cut broke the fetcher because 'is not False' read silence as a candidate, and a test caught it, so it asks candidate_issues instead. The sequencing tile says which of three states each field is in via editmeta, sampled from a board epic and shown beside a refusal only. docs/forge-deployment.md gains the field setup.

nodes.label: 1.68.0 — An epic can carry a t-shirt size, and the sequencer stops treating every ask as the same size
nodes.rationale: ADR 0029: tshirt_scale builds S/M/L/XL from quartiles of the epics this board has completed, so a band selects a reference class and asserts no number, which separates it from estimating in points (ADR 0006). Banded and unbanded asks mix in one comparison, each row carrying sizing_method and sizing_basis shown in a Sized by column. Three answers: the four bands, absent, and anything else falling back to the whole class and named. Costs eight completed epics. orgConfig.sizeField resolves like askField. Both implementations run over shared cases in tests/forge_shapes.mjs. Deployed as 7.7.0.

nodes.label: 1.67.0 — The value and its basis are on the page
nodes.rationale: Item 7 slice four: sequence had put value and valueBasis on every ordering row and nothing read them. The tile leads with what each ask is worth, why, and when it is needed, beside the ordering cost; nothing sorts or scores on it (ADR 0004, ADR 0027). An unpriced ask says Not priced. Disclosures render beside refusals as well as answers (ADR 0028). Two shape bugs found by rendering: serve_live.py added asks_considered, board and boardName that the resolver did not, and the page carried a loopback-specific data/asks/ sentence, now neutral. Pinned in tests/e2e.py over a Forge-shaped body with hostile titles escaped.

nodes.label: 1.66.1 — Both transports looked for candidates in the one place a candidate cannot be
nodes.rationale: Epics are fetched separately and kept when they finished inside the period, right for value (ADR 0026) and wrong for candidacy, since a candidate has no resolution date; every one was excluded, always. An epic is kept when it finished in the window or has been reached for, unreadable answers included. Sixty-five facts figures were compared before and after and only the counting disclosure moved (ADR 0024, ADR 0026). The resolver referenced a bare `as` that node --check cannot see; it is asUser now. The live board finds both candidates and refuses for want of history.

nodes.label: 1.66.0 — The Forge sequencing refusal is gone
nodes.rationale: Item 7 slice three: the resolver assembles candidates and delegates to /v1/sequence, computing nothing. Candidacy is decided inside the tenant because an unreadable answer is free text, so forge/src/jira.js gains candidateAnswer, candidateIssues and asksFromIssues run against the Python over shared cases. Only an id, a sizing method, an amount and a date cross. assertNoFreeText guarded projected issues but an ask is built, so /v1/sequence and /v1/ask accepted titles; assertAsksCarryNoText in the resolver and _refuse_ask_text in the service close that door. Two refusals: nothing marked, and one marked. Deployed as 7.5.0.

nodes.label: 1.65.0 — A declared candidate becomes an ask
nodes.rationale: Item 7 slice two: intake.asks_from_issues() assembles the shape sequence and readiness consume out of a Jira board. title and team are the summary and board, sizing is reference-class, valueEstimate is the two declared fields (ADR 0025, ADR 0027) present or absent never half, neededBy is dueDate; the raw businessValue is read rather than value_of because nothing is summed. A delivered candidate is still a candidate (ADR 0028). Proved end to end over a real board. Limitation stated: reference-class sizing gives every ask the same distribution.

nodes.label: 1.64.0 — The Forge build had lost the coloured half of itself, and it looked like a design decision
nodes.rationale: A Custom UI iframe's style-src without unsafe-inline silently discards every style attribute the renderers write (155 on the sample sprint): bars kept their track and lost their fill, discs lost their colour. Fixed in src/app.js by testing a style attribute on a detached element at startup and, where it did not survive, wrapping the innerHTML setter once to re-apply via el.style.cssText, which the CSSOM permits; relaxing the manifest policy was rejected. Pinned in e2e.py by serving the page under a real style-src 'self' header and without, requiring identical results. ADR 0008 carries the finding.

nodes.label: 1.63.0 — Something in Jira can now say 'this is being weighed against other things'
nodes.rationale: Item 7 slice one, ADR 0028: candidacy is a state, not a type, because sequencing on issue type would order decisions already taken. orgConfig.askField defaults to app (the declared Candidate field) or names a site's own checkbox or select by id then display name. Forge cannot declare a checkbox and the app cannot create one (Administer Jira, refused by ADR 0020 and 0021), so the app's field is text. Three answers: Yes/Y/True, empty, and anything else returned as written by candidate_answer and named by the caller. Read on both transports; the projection guard extends to candidate. Deployed as 7.3.0; Jira creates the field about a minute after deploy.

nodes.label: 1.62.0 — The fetcher reads the two fields this app declares, and fetches the issues that carry them
nodes.rationale: The fetcher wrote businessValue: 0 and valueBasis: '' on every issue, so the file route reported every board as worth nothing; metrics keys measured-from-unmeasured on the key's presence, so zero was a stronger false claim than absence. The key is omitted when the site has no field and null when unfilled. Matched on the module key, never display name. Epics are fetched separately for those finishing in the period (ADR 0026) on both pull paths. Three states, three sentences (ADR 0025). Proved against live Jira (MOBL-2, US$40,000 with its basis) and driven through a stub transport in test_agent.py.

nodes.label: 1.61.0 — A reader who knows the board can now say what each status means
nodes.rationale: The Workflow chip becomes answerable: the answer goes into the dataset's own orgConfig.statuses and Save a copy carries it, rather than a view toggle that would let two readers of one file see different figures and that has nowhere to live without browser storage. normaliseIssue keeps the producer's statusCategory, so applying a mapping re-derives from the dataset as it arrived. It offers the board's statuses, transition targets included. workflowSetBy records the statement so nothing is reported as inferred over a stated answer; reset returns to the file; nothing is written to the tracker. Pinned in e2e.py.

nodes.label: 1.60.0 — The dashboard now says which statuses its config did not name
nodes.rationale: An unrecognised status reads as To Do and flattens the burndown; the fetcher printed the names once to a terminal. A Workflow chip appears only when something was inferred and names each status, its reading and evidence; the footer repeats it because the chip does not print. The fetcher writes orgConfig.inferredStatuses and the page records its own on Forge, the producer's entry winning. orgconfig.Statuses ranks evidence rather than last-write-wins (the first cut understated Jira's own classification). unmatched and inferred are kept as different questions. Names are escaped. Pinned in test_agent.py and e2e.py; the live board reports two.

nodes.label: 1.59.0 — The page dropped four of the organisation's own settings and used its defaults instead
nodes.rationale: orgConfigOf() named four keys and discarded everything else a dataset stated, despite its comment claiming to merge like the Python; countSubtasks, countedTypes, valueFromHierarchy and trendSprints never reached the page, so a site setting countSubtasks: true got two throughputs, both looking right. Live on Forge too, since mergeOrgConfig preserved them. e2e's non-default check had overridden only the calendar; it now moves all four, compares the whole merged config to orgconfig.merge() key for key, and asserts countedIssues (exported on window.DVD) acts on the value. Found by reading the path a value takes, not by a test.

nodes.label: 1.58.1 — Accepted is stated rather than inferred
nodes.rationale: The first real pull reported three statuses matched by no rule and resolved from Jira's category; Accepted is confirmed In Progress, so config/organisation.json says so rather than relying on a fallback that was right by luck.

nodes.label: 1.58.0 — The fetcher made its first real request to a Jira, and three things were wrong that no stub could have shown
nodes.rationale: /rest/api/3/field answers 200 to an anonymous caller, so a bad credential did not fail: find_fields found no story-point field, warned, and continued with every issue at zero points, a flattened burndown behind one warning line. Jira.whoami() and _verified() now prove the connection is somebody before any data call, on both transports; the story-point warning vanished the moment auth worked. secret_checks flagged .env three lines below the check asserting it is git-ignored; the scan now asks git for tracked plus untracked files it would add. .env.example's unquoted ORG_NAME broke sourcing. 1.56.0's token paging was proven against the real API (pages of 10/10/10/8, 38 collected) rather than argued.

nodes.label: 1.57.1 — The cost stated in 1.57.0 was wrong, and the deploy is what said so
nodes.rationale: The Value Basis field deployed as 7.2.0 with no MAJOR_VERSION_RULE approval and no forge install --upgrade. Introducing a module type is major; adding an entry to a block already declared is minor; scope changes stay major. ADR 0025's over-broad 'declaring a module always is' is corrected where it was written. Caught by doing the thing rather than reasoning about it, the same pattern as the defects found by looking in 1.36.0-1.56.0.

nodes.label: 1.57.0 — The app declares a Value Basis field, and it is free text on purpose
nodes.rationale: ADR 0027: sequence prints each ask's basis beside the computable delivery consequence and computes nothing on it; an enumeration is one join from a table of weights and the priority score ADR 0004 refuses. Not read from the description, because 'no basis recorded' must stay sayable for readiness (the ADR 0010 shape). issueFields and both fetchers now take one named {value, basis} pair resolved by a single field read, since two adjacent positional ids transposed would fail silently in both directions; both finders match on module key and test_service asserts neither key is a substring of the other. A non-string basis reads as absent. The field is requested, not merely read. The sequence refusal names one remaining cause. The stated major-version cost was wrong (corrected in 1.57.1). Nothing new crosses: valueBasis was already in NEVER_SEND and FREE_TEXT_FIELDS.

nodes.label: 1.56.3 — The second stale line in the same risks section, found by reading the rest of it after fixing the first
nodes.rationale: docs/roadmap.md's risks said item 3 'is what is being built' four days after delivery. Phase 3 was built before any engagement signal existed (one installation, development, on the dev site), and the reason it was not deferred never depended on the signal: without phase 3 the product cannot pass a security review. The open half is whether item 3 is what customers value.

nodes.label: 1.56.2 — docs/roadmap.md said item 5 had not started, four hundred lines after saying it had
nodes.rationale: The state table said First pass done while the risks section said untested. The risk itself, plan against the upper bound, is unchanged: ADRs 0018-0020 answered three exposures by accepting and naming disclosures, which is a coherent position and not the permission model the 5-8 weeks estimated, so none of that estimate has been spent.

nodes.label: 1.56.1 — ADR 0026 was referenced in five places and had never been written
nodes.rationale: Comments in orgconfig.py, metrics.py, src/app.js and forge/src/index.js, two changelog entries and a manifest comment pointed at it. It exists now, recording that epics are not on a scrum board and that items and value are counted from two sets; a sweep of ADR NNNN references against docs/adr/ reports none missing. docs/roadmap.md records item 7's roll-up done and the Marketplace gaps.

nodes.label: 1.56.0 — The fetcher called an endpoint Atlassian has removed, and the migration was not a URL swap
nodes.rationale: /rest/api/3/search is removed in favour of /search/jql, which pages by token and returns no total; changing only the path would have made body.get('total', 0) end the loop after one page, one hundred issues reported as the whole board. The walk ends on the absence of a token and on isLast; with no total to check against, the page cap raises rather than returning a partial board. Tested through a stub transport: three token pages, isLast honoured, a single page, startAt never sent, changelog still expanded, an endless token stream raising at the cap.

nodes.label: 1.55.1 — The value tile printed '-1 of the 0 completed items carry no value estimate'
nodes.rationale: Items and value are two sets (ADR 0026) and this line subtracted the value pool from the item pool. Both sides now come from the value pool, the note says where value is recorded, and openDrill reads the value pool first because clicking a value row threw. Pinned in tests/e2e.py, which asserts no negative count and no zero denominator.

nodes.label: 1.55.0 — Business value on an epic reached nothing, because epics are not on a scrum board
nodes.rationale: The sprint issue endpoint never returns an epic, so a priced Done epic was never fetched (ADR 0026). The board's epics are fetched separately (1 + E calls, capped and reported) and credited to the period they finished in. Items and value are two pools: an epic is excluded from item counts for the subtask reason, but it is the only place value is recorded, so counted_issues and value_issues are separate sets read by facts, history_row and the page. history_row was counting an epic as an item because it never applied the item rule. read:epic:jira-software added to the scope allow-list, found by forge lint. Separately recorded: the fetcher's /rest/api/3/search is removed by Atlassian.

nodes.label: 1.54.1 — The Business Value field was declared, read, and never requested
nodes.rationale: businessValue was in the projection but not in issueFields, so Jira sent it on no issue and every value came back absent with no error, for the length of one deploy. Both fetch paths request it and test_service holds projection and request together while keeping the fields named. Found by reading what the board fetch asks Jira for, not by a test.

nodes.label: 1.54.0 — The app declares a Business Value field, so a Forge tenant can report value for the first time
nodes.rationale: ADR 0025: a jira:customField module makes Jira create the field on install, needing no Administer Jira (refused by ADR 0020 and 0021) and no write scope. Found by key, never display name (findStoryPointField deliberately differs); unset is null not 0. Counted at epic level and above only, via orgConfig.valueFromHierarchy = 1 over Jira's hierarchy as a level rather than a type list. Three empty-tile sentences. Costs: a major version (later refined) and business value reaching the calculator as a bare number. Three guards caught it: projection parity, invents-no-field until hierarchyLevel was justified, and the store inventory which now follows kvs calls to their literals.

nodes.label: 1.53.0 — An issue-type filter that changes what the dashboard counts, not only what it lists
nodes.rationale: Types are read off the loaded issues with counts. The selection travels with the forecast and is in fcKey and the loopback cache key, or tiles and forecast would count different sets. A reader narrows the organisation's rule via an effective config so counted_issues stays the one implementation; uncounted types are not offered. Selecting nothing is a refusal (ADR 0010). Native checkboxes. It exposed an older bug: dropdowns built once under dataset.built and never rebuilt on a board switch, so a second board offered the first board's people and epics; keyed on their options now. Pinned in tests/e2e.py.

nodes.label: 1.52.0 — Subtasks were counted as items everywhere, and nothing recorded that they were
nodes.rationale: Every item-denominated figure counted subtasks, so decomposing generously inflated throughput exactly as estimating generously would, and whether subtasks arrived varied by board type and route with nothing on screen saying which. countSubtasks defaults false and countedTypes is an allow-list defaulting to empty, validated in Python and mirrored in forge/src/jira.js (ADR 0024). Jira's own flag, and absence is not subtask. facts.meta.counting and forecast.inputs.counting always report what was seen and counted. Guards caught it: projection parity needed type and isSubtask in CALC_FIELDS, and parentKey was rejected as read by nothing.

nodes.label: 1.51.0 — The cross-team roll-up is wired, and wiring it found two bugs, one of them older than this feature
nodes.rationale: selectContext skipped fetching for a roll-up, so one selected before its sprints were opened counted a subset while its header counted them all, a fault the per-board roll-up has had since live mode existed; members are fetched on selection and failures named. The fix's trap: loadContext ended S.ctx = id, so filling a roll-up moved the reader; it takes a select argument. The roll-up is offered as '- all boards -' and names its boards (ADR 0023). forecast_for's top-level refusal rendered as a shrug; it now refuses in the noCalculator shape. Both pinned in tests/e2e.py.

nodes.label: 1.50.0 — Roadmap item 7 is started, and its stated blocker was wrong about both halves
nodes.rationale: ADR 0023: sequencing is already built and refuses on Forge only because nobody decided what an ask is inside Jira, unrelated to items 4 and 5. rollteams:<projectKey> spans boards and is deliberately not a variant of roll:. The roll-up names the boards it covers because the app cannot know which boards it is not seeing (reading as the app is kept off the panel path by ADR 0018). It reports facts and refuses to forecast, for two reasons kept apart: team_slice would narrow silently (the 1.8.0 fault), and pooling teams' throughput is a modelling error. Windows are excluded.

nodes.label: 1.49.0 — SSO needed nothing built, and item 6 is done
nodes.rationale: ADR 0022: the app owns no identity, so the customer's IdP policy governs completely. The suite checks what would falsify that: no password, token, Authorization or Basic auth in forge/src, no cookie or session, no auth module, no environment credential in the installed app. The one IdP-bypass path, JIRA_TOKEN in scripts/fetch_delivery_data.py, is confined to scripts/. A check failed on a comment naming process.env.CALCULATOR_URL (ADR 0012) and now reads code not prose. Item 6's three features cost far less than the 6-10 weeks estimated, said plainly in the roadmap.

nodes.label: 1.48.0 — The activity log is built, and it is called an activity log because that is what it is
nodes.rationale: ADR 0021: four events in app storage shown to administrators. The roadmap's dependency on item 5 was wrong; the real constraint is that Jira's audit API is read-only and reading it needs Administer Jira (refused by ADR 0020), so an app-written log is not tamper-evident and the tile, auditNote and tests say so. Bounded at a thousand with a cumulative droppedTotal in the store. Counts, flags, field names and the actor; a write never fails the act it records. Two guards caught it: the store inventory needed audit declared, and a team-label check tripped on entry.team.users. What a security review asks for, a record the app could not falsify, needs a customer-controlled sink (ADR 0013's mechanism, a larger crossing).

nodes.label: 1.47.0 — The anchor issue is the brief's access control, and saying so closes item 5's first pass
nodes.rationale: ADR 0020 names the mechanism that existed: an administrator chooses the anchor and Jira enforces browse permission at send time (ADR 0014). The residual aggregate leak is accepted as strictly weaker than the stores' exposure. The investigation corrected ADR 0018: per-recipient composition is not 'a different product' but Forge's offline impersonation (api.asUser(accountId) with allowImpersonation), deferred for three stated reasons. Checking recipients via /permissions/check was refused (Administer Jira). test_service fails if the manifest declares allowImpersonation or an administer-Jira grant. Item 5 is a first pass, not done.

nodes.label: 1.46.0 — The forecast log is the board's too, and the asymmetry with a sprint row decided the design
nodes.rationale: A claim is made once and resolved once, never rescored, so the irreversible hazard is resolving a good claim from a view that cannot see the work. Two gates: a claim narrower than the log's widest view is not published and the reader is told; a claim is left pending when the resolving view is narrower than the making view. Claims with no recorded width still resolve. calibration_note's refusal branch returned early and left the held-back sentence unsaid; both branches carry it. The brief remains item 5's open exposure (ADR 0018).

nodes.label: 1.45.0 — A recorded sprint row belongs to the board, and that decision has teeth
nodes.rationale: ADR 0019 answers the question ADR 0018 left: the aggregate disclosure under issue-level security is accepted (a count, never a title, as ADR 0015 and 0017 required). A row written by a narrow reader is wrong, not merely leaky, so a row records issuesSeen and three rules follow: a narrower view never replaces a row, a wider view corrects one (the single exception to ADR 0015's never-rewrite), and a reader who sees less is told so. Such rows are excluded from ADR 0015's disagreement sentence. Thirteen cases in tests/fixtures/series-cases.json hold both transports. The forecast log is deliberately not folded in.

nodes.label: 1.44.0 — Roadmap item 5 is started, and it starts by finding two exposures this repository created yesterday
nodes.rationale: ADR 0018 surveys and fixes nothing: the panel mirrors permissions by property (every read is api.asUser()), but the durable series stores what one viewer could see and shows it to everyone, and the forecast log has the same shape; item 4a converted a property into an assumption unnoticed from 1.36.0 through 1.43.0. This collides with ADR 0015's keep-both decision and is written down as a deliberate reversal to come. The brief leaks less than ADR 0013 and the roadmap implied: briefMessages hands the model only figures. Every app-level store is declared with what it exposes, orgConfig included though a project property. Two checks were wrong first: resolving the forecastLogKey function instead of its literal, and scanning only index.js.

nodes.label: 1.43.0 — The trend window is a setting, and both of its truncations now say what they cut; roadmap item 4 is done
nodes.rationale: Three producers each kept a silent six (build_history in the fetcher, upto[-6:] in the sample generator, SPRINTS_PER_BOARD in the resolver), the silent cap CLAUDE.md forbids. trendSprints travels in the resolved config, default six, bounded two to forty, held together by orgconfig.validate and its forge/src/jira.js mirror over shared cases. merge_series reported every recorded sprint outside the window as 'no longer offered', false on any board deeper than its window; outside-the-window and missing-from-inside are separated with different remedies. A board deeper than its window says so. data/sample-bundle.json regenerates byte for byte.

nodes.label: 1.42.0 — The forecast log is wired, and the forecaster is falsifiable for the first time
nodes.rationale: Item 4c done: a published forecast writes capacity claims to the board's log (app storage on Forge, a git-ignored file over loopback) and the tile prints how it has done. A what-if writes nothing, because claim_id keyed on context, day and percentile would overwrite a real claim; forecast_for emits claims for the default forecast alone. update_log adds, resolves, trims and scores in one tool function, held byte for byte by test_service. Resolution runs at each transport's own as-of (today on Forge, the file's end over loopback). Bounded at four hundred with pending claims never dropped and the count reported; written only when moved. Ten resolved forecasts are needed before a Brier score, and the scorer's refusal is printed verbatim.

nodes.label: 1.41.0 — The forecaster can be scored against its own history now, for the first time
nodes.rationale: Item 4c started: score_calibration had a reader and nothing ever produced a log. claims_from, resolve_claims and problems_in_claim sit beside it in forecast.py; the last of twenty-six checks scores a produced log end to end. ADR 0017: a forecast is logged as capacity claims ('p% confidence of at least N items by D') that resolve from a count and hold no issue identity, keeping item 4 off item 5's permission model; CLAIM_FIELDS is an allow-list. A refusal is not logged. Claim ids are deterministic so eleven panel loads are one observation. Resolved once over (madeOn, horizon] and never rescored. Two limits recorded: correlated claims overstate n, and moved work resolves false (ADR 0015's gap). Nothing writes the log yet.

nodes.label: 1.40.2 — docs/roadmap.md records item 4 as part done, and defines the letters the entries below have been using
nodes.rationale: 4a is the store (done, in a tenant), 4b the window, 4c the forecast log; the decomposition is of the work, not the roadmap's numbering. Entries 1.36.0 through 1.38.0 called the store 4b; both the roadmap and ADR 0015 put the store first, so they are corrected in place with the correction recorded here rather than made silently.

nodes.label: 1.40.1 — The same false basis, in the next clause of the same sentence
nodes.rationale: 1.40.0 fixed the phrase carrying the figure and left 'rather than a mean of three numbers' two lines later about the same one-sprint average. Both read off recentAvgN and tests/e2e.py asserts the phrase is absent as well as the figure being right.

nodes.label: 1.40.0 — Three things a two-sprint board made visible
nodes.rationale: The predictability tile claimed 'the last three actuals' whatever the history held; hist.slice(-4, -1) yields one entry on a two-sprint board, presented as a three-sprint average. recentAvg and recentAvgN (renamed from avg3) travel together and every sentence states its basis, pinned by rendering one- and two-sprint histories from file://. The caption 'last six sprints' was a cap, now 'sprint by sprint'. contextEntry reported asOfDate: null, so a Forge series rested on endDate and dated closed sprints to their planned end; it now resolves as scripts/fetch_delivery_data.py does (today running, completion finished, planned end only without a completion), held equal in test_service over five sprints. A wrong comment on contextBody's fallback is corrected.

nodes.label: 1.39.2 — A sprint the series could not date left it silently, and the tile blamed thin data
nodes.rationale: history_series skipped any context it could not date, with a comment claiming the caller counted them; nothing counted them, the silent cap CLAUDE.md forbids. skipped_note() names every context that produced no row (no end date and no as-of, a flow window per ADR 0011, no id) and the route reports offered beside sprints. The page distinguishes 'could not measure', printing the server's sentence, from 'not enough sprints', stating how many the board offers. contextEntry's asOfDate: null divergence is left standing for its own change.

nodes.label: 1.39.1 — The trend was empty in the tenant, and the cause was a sort order
nodes.rationale: series_upto truncates by position and the two callers disagreed about order: a bundle lists sprints oldest first, the Forge resolver's recentSprints newest first, so selecting the newest sprint truncated the series to one row on Forge, what ADR 0009 exists to prevent. history_series sorts by start date with undated contexts last, and series_upto narrows to the selected board. The thin-data sentence had been printed for four causes; each has its own words and both tiles hand their sentence in. The e2e parity check feeds both transports the same loopback contexts so could not see it; pinned in test_service by running one board's contexts both ways.

nodes.label: 1.39.0 — The calculator image takes Debian's security updates at build time, and deploys move again
nodes.rationale: Every push since 2026-08-28 failed service/scan.sh on three fixable findings from one OpenSSL CVE with a published fix, so item 4a could not reach a tenant. The failure was misread twice as the gate blocking on unfixable findings; it already runs --ignore-unfixed and was telling the truth. No base image fixed it (3.12-slim, 3.13-slim, alpine all failed on the same CVE; distroless scanned worse), so apt upgrade, never dist-upgrade, in the build takes Debian's patch: three fixable before, none after, 52.6 to 56.5 MB. Suppressing via a Trivy ignore was refused. ADR 0016 has the measurements; hosting doc section 11 gains a section on a red scan.

nodes.label: 1.38.1 — The fetcher is importable again without a tracker dependency, and CI is what found it
nodes.rationale: fetch_delivery_data.py called sys.exit() at import when requests was absent, and 1.38.0 made tests/test_agent.py import it; every developer machine has requests, the CI runner does not. need_requests() prints the sentence at the point of use. Pinned by importing in a subprocess with requests genuinely blocked, because a function existing says nothing about whether the import still exits.

nodes.label: 1.38.0 — A Forge tenant has a trend at last
nodes.rationale: Item 4a wired: history rows come from a route of their own on both transports (the history resolver, api/history over loopback), one set of shapes (ADR 0009), rather than a field on the single-sprint context body. seriesNote in forge/src/series.js counted rows into a sentence, arithmetic between tool and reader, so merge_series, series_disagreements and series_note moved to agent/tools/metrics.py; series.js keeps storage policy, run over one case file by test_service. The served route answered for the whole board, so a June sprint drew a trend through September; series_upto() in the tool slices to the selection, caught by the transport-parity check in tests/e2e.py. Rebuilt points draw hollow and dashed with provenance on hover; valueDelivered is absent not nil over the calculator; problemsInRow allows null in two positions; --info-wash replaced by --info-ink; trend tiles print the served reason before the thin-data sentence, ordered by tests/security.py. No new scope (storage:app, ADR 0014); loopback store data/series.local.json.

nodes.label: 1.37.0 — The durable series has a module and a shape, and neither of them stores an issue
nodes.rationale: Item 4a: forge/src/series.js is pure and owns what is kept, what may be written, and how a recorded row and a re-derived one present side by side; forty-four checks in test_service. ROW_FIELDS and rowProjection follow people.js: nine numbers and a sprint name, problemsInRow refusing rather than trimming, which keeps item 4 off item 5's critical path. recordable() implements ADR 0015: an active sprint is observed, a watched sprint recorded when it closes, a sprint closed before the app saw the board shown and not stored; a post-close row is never rewritten. Disagreements keep both rows and name the fields. Rows carry a fingerprint of the statuses they were computed under. history_row moved from the fetcher into agent/tools/metrics.py because the calculator ships agent/tools only. Not wired yet.

nodes.label: 1.36.0 — A closed sprint got better the longer ago it was, and nothing on screen said so
nodes.rationale: Every history row derived completion and work in progress from an issue's current status, facts about the fetch rather than the sprint, so old sprints reported no WIP and full commitment. Rows are now derived from dates keyed to the sprint's asOfDate. Four implementations of the row collapse into history_row(). Both fixture generators wrote issues done after the as-of; clamped. Two security checks pinned generated numbers rather than a relationship. ADR 0015 settles item 4: store only what Jira forgets (a published forecast, a deleted issue, commitment after sprint membership is stripped, status-dependent figures); the first draft wrongly held wipItems irrecoverable; started is the changelog replayed through today's orgConfig; the store comes first and the window second.

nodes.label: 1.35.0 — The read-only view of the recipients tile shows names too, which is the surface 1.34.0 said it had not fixed
nodes.rationale: A non-administrator sees the configuration and cannot change it, an argument that only works if the recipients are legible; the ids are resolved one row per id with name, state and id. Users and groups are separate facts. Ids are never lost when the lookup cannot answer. showBriefNames is a separate projection rather than a flag on wireBriefNames, and never calls render(). picker_checks() gains the fourth render path. docs/roadmap.md's 'Item 3, which is next' section is replaced with what is open.

nodes.label: 1.34.0 — The account-ID field is folded away, and the named list is where recipients are edited
nodes.rationale: Seen in a tenant, an administrator met a box demanding an account id before anything readable. The named list is primary with a remove control per row and the field sits behind an Account IDs disclosure that both lookups open when there is no directory. Removal is by account id, not position, so duplicates cannot leave a phantom recipient. Nothing calls render(); the list leaves the live region; focus lands sensibly. A display name now reaches an aria-label attribute, so picker_checks() asserts esc() escapes both quote characters. The read-only view was not fixed here (1.35.0).

nodes.label: 1.33.0 — The recipient field shows who those ids are
nodes.rationale: Ids are resolved to names via GET /rest/api/3/user/bulk under read:jira-user, no new scope. The names are a gloss beside the ids, never over them. Three states (active, deactivated, unknown) because the fixes differ; deactivated accounts are shown here and filtered from the search. user/bulk omits unmatched ids, so they are recovered per id rather than by counting. The note says nothing when nothing is wrong. route takes a URLSearchParams and test_service fails if assumeTrustedRoute ever appears. No render(); refresh on blur; the newest lookup wins over a slower one. A second render path for the untrusted name is covered by picker_checks(). The search was used by a person on the dev site.

nodes.label: 1.32.0 — A brief was delivered; roadmap item 3 is done
nodes.rationale: Outgoing mail was switched on for the site and the next fire sent (2026-08-26); Jira's errorMessages had said 'Outgoing emails disabled' all along and the app was discarding them. The recipient picker takes a name via searchUsers; the field stays the thing that is saved; nothing in the picker calls render() because the tile is a half-filled form; Enter searches rather than submitting. Display names are escaped through the one esc() with a structural picker_checks() in tests/security.py, since loopback has no directory. Not verified by eye, because synthetic scrolling does not reach the frame.

nodes.label: 1.31.0 — The recipient picker takes a name, not an account id
nodes.rationale: searchUsers looks a name up and the picker stores the id. This is not what ADR 0014 refuses: a human picks from Jira's matches rather than the app resolving an email address. The search runs as the reader so Jira's Browse users and groups permission decides, with a 403 said in those words. Each match is an allow-list of two fields (the shape of the calculator's clean_dataset); deactivated, app and customer accounts are filtered. A shown count was Math.min recomputed rather than read off the list and is people.length now. Loopback says it has no directory rather than returning nobody. The dev site's outgoing mail is off since 18 August.

nodes.label: 1.30.0 — Item 3 runs end to end against a real tenant, and the only thing between it and an inbox is a site setting
nodes.rationale: Jira refused with 403 'Outgoing emails disabled', which ADR 0014 records as a Marketplace precondition. Six failures fixed with tests: per-board reasons unlogged, composeSection discarding proseFrom's cause, sendBrief discarding errorMessages; 'stop' is OpenAI's word and Anthropic ends with end_turn, so FINISHED, TRUNCATED and DECLINED are explicit lists and an unknown value is refused and named; a model refusal is its own category; the slot key p85 made the model write 85, so no slot name contains a digit and a failing section is retried once; sectionsFor was written against the flat /v1/forecast shape while /v1/forecast-context nests under sprint_completion, and the test now takes shapes from the real tool. Four came from coding against examples rather than the SDK's types. Mutation testing measured by grep -c FAIL was lying; exit status now. ADR 0013's guard fired on live output and sent nothing.

nodes.label: 1.29.5 — There was no bug: the dashboard scrolls on Forge with a mouse, and 1.29.1 through 1.29.4 were chasing an artefact of how it was being tested
nodes.rationale: Confirmed by a person with a hand on a mouse. The measurements were correct (frame 1040px, document 1498px), the third clause 'and it does not scroll' was never established: synthetic wheel and key events do not reach a cross-origin iframe, and the automation's coordinate space shifted between screenshots. Three fixes were designed and reverted (view.resize(), layout: blank, view.emitReadyEvent()) across app versions 6.2.0 to 6.8.0. The rule now in docs/forge-deployment.md: a negative result from synthetic input against an embedded frame is not evidence. The recipients tile was always reachable.

nodes.label: 1.29.4 — view.emitReadyEvent() changed nothing
nodes.rationale: Third host-side candidate eliminated at 4, 10 and 16 seconds; reverted to 6.8.0. More importantly, every 'it does not scroll' result came from synthetic input and at least one demonstrably went to the host document (a 78px nav collapse), so the state of knowledge is a table: the frame height and document height are measured, a real reader's inability to scroll is not established. A .wrap element-scroller fix was written and reverted unproven.

nodes.label: 1.29.3 — 1.29.2 was wrong, and this measures the thing both previous entries argued about
nodes.rationale: The frame's document loaded standalone from its CDN URL is 1498px, overflow visible, not constrained, which is what 1.29.1 said. The false correction came from a shifted screenshot coordinate space, so scroll and click coordinates were not landing where they appeared; the lesson is that a negative result from synthetic input against an embedded frame is worthless without checking the coordinate space. The host performs Custom UI resizing and nothing in the SDK sizes the app's frame; view.emitReadyEvent() is the untested candidate, not shipped.

nodes.label: 1.29.2 — layout: blank was the next hypothesis for the clipped Forge iframe, and it is wrong too
nodes.rationale: jira:projectPage has no viewportSize; layout: blank deployed as 6.4.0 recovered only the chrome's height (1016px) and was reverted in 6.5.0. Testing it suggested (wrongly, per 1.29.3) that the content was constrained rather than overflowing; a .wrap scroll container is written down as the next experiment rather than built, and docs/forge-deployment.md says to compare scrollHeight against the frame height first.

nodes.label: 1.29.1 — The scheduled trigger runs the new code, and the deploy is proved
nodes.rationale: App 6.0.0 reinstalled after the scope change; with interval fiveMinute the handler refused through problemsIn at INFO, proving the trigger fires under 6.x and reads app storage; restored to week as 6.3.0. It found what looked like a real bug: the Custom UI iframe at 1040px with overflow clip and a host page that would not scroll (later shown in 1.29.5 to be a testing artefact). A view.resize() fix was reverted because the SDK's types show view has no resize method. The no-silent-caps rule fired on PLAT's 2659 sprints, and the dashboard rendered real tenant numbers for the first time.

nodes.label: 1.29.0 — The scheduled brief reads the board and sends it; item 3 is built end to end
nodes.rationale: This reverses ADR 0013's addendum declining asApp(), and the record says so: every notification now carries restrict {BROWSE}, so who may receive a brief is Jira's decision; the residual issue-level-security risk is stated in both records. jira(as) replaces nine api.asUser() call sites, defaulted to the user, with the scheduled path passing 'app' at every hop; two reads may never take it. A structural test walks every jira(as) to a function declaring `as`, because the same free-variable ReferenceError appeared twice (editabilityFor and the context resolver) and bundles cleanly. sectionsFor chooses figures and does no arithmetic; items_done_pct is deliberately unused. Unproven in a tenant.

nodes.label: 1.28.0 — Each board now has its own recipients, set from the dashboard by a project administrator
nodes.rationale: A new tile reads the configuration over whichever transport and writes it back through the one mutating route. permissions.js asks /rest/api/3/mypermissions for ADMINISTER_PROJECTS and accepts exactly true, asked again on the write. Non-administrators see the configuration. The tile validates nothing. serve_live.py mirrors the validation, held to the Forge one over tests/fixtures/recipient-configs.json (nineteen cases, verdicts compared, the email-address message pinned separately). Saving is a POST over loopback with LIVE.put hiding the asymmetry (ADR 0009). The route-parity test now derives ROUTES from src/app.js and checks serve_live.py serves each. Found by looking: the stylesheet used tokens that do not exist, giving white borders silently.

nodes.label: 1.27.0 — The brief is an email now, and the send is written and proved against stubs
nodes.rationale: mailbody.js renders subject, textBody and htmlBody; compose.js takes figures to a sent message; index.js posts to /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/notify as the app. Two defences: esc() character for character the one in src/app.js, held by a test, and safeUrl(); and header injection, since a board name with CRLF would close the Subject, so subjects are flattened, C0-stripped and capped at 200. Mutation testing showed the fixture never exercised the escape on section bodies. Prose carrying a figure sends nothing; an invalid config sends nothing; refused sections are carried verbatim; one audience failing does not block the other; restrict is built inside notifyPayload. asApp() is deliberately not taken (ADR 0013) and the handler refuses at that point. compose.js exists for testability. An assertion matching a comment now strips comments first.

nodes.label: 1.26.0 — Jira sends the brief, so item 3 crosses no boundary at all
nodes.rationale: ADR 0014: POST /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/notify sends through Jira's own machinery. Recipients are Jira identities; recipients.js refuses email addresses rather than resolving them. A constant restrict {BROWSE} is the only platform-enforced permission filter here and is partial (anchor issue only; item 5). The cost is attachments, so the view ships as static HTML. The read-only scope rule becomes an allow-list with a justification in the manifest for send:notification:jira and storage:app, stricter than the prefix check. A Jira project property as config home was rejected. Project administrators decide recipients via /mypermissions. Validation refusals each correspond to a silent failure and are mutation-tested. forge lint: one MAJOR_VERSION_RULE approval, a reinstall.

nodes.label: 1.25.2 — The handler runs, and it refuses exactly as written
nodes.rationale: interval fiveMinute deployed as 5.2.0 fired three times to the second at INFO, reaching index.weeklyBrief and refusing with all three blockers in order; restored to week as 5.3.0, a minor change. This corrects 1.25.1's two explanations for silence (a disabled trigger or the scope change), both now excluded: the silence was a weekly interval that was not due. An absence of logs cannot distinguish broken from idle, so docs/forge-deployment.md says to establish liveness by shortening the interval. The 1.25.1 diagnosis was a plausible story fitted to missing data, the project's worst failure mode arriving in a changelog entry.

nodes.label: 1.25.1 — App version 5.0.0 is deployed to the dev site, and the platform confirmed the claim ADR 0013 rests on
nodes.rationale: forge lint passed the llm module with one MAJOR_VERSION_RULE approval; forge eligibility at 5.0.0 reports only the calculator's two findings, so the Atlassian-hosted model adds no egress (ADR 0008's badge trade unchanged). A module upgrade takes via forge install --upgrade where a scope change does not, despite a misleading warning; the runbook separates them. Two trigger fires on 2026-08-24 failed with the functionKey TypeError, confirming 1.25.0's prediction with timestamps; then zero invocations in thirty-one hours, recorded as unexplained with two candidate causes (both excluded in 1.25.2). A fresh install changed the installation ARI.

nodes.label: 1.25.0 — The llm module is declared and the weekly brief has a handler, and wiring it found the trigger had been failing on every fire
nodes.rationale: weekly-brief pointed at the resolver function, whose getDefinitions() dispatcher expects {call: {functionKey}}; it has its own function, weekly-brief-fn and index.weeklyBrief, with a test holding the two apart. forge lint reports one MAJOR_VERSION_RULE for core:llm, ADR 0013's predicted cost. A scheduled send has no user and every read is api.asUser(); asApp() is the wrong repair because reading as the user is what makes permission mirroring hold, so item 3 depends on item 5 and the roadmap now says so; assertions keep asUser() out of the trigger body. It refuses with three sentences before any Jira call. The pipeline is deliberately not written against imagined shapes. Figures reach the model as named values, refused figures are named but their sentences withheld, truncated completions are discarded, and the manifest checks read without PyYAML.

nodes.label: 1.24.1 — Editing a README redeployed both Cloud Run regions, and now it does not
nodes.rationale: deploy.yml filtered on service/**, so a service/README.md edit shipped the calculator twice. service/**.md is excluded because the Dockerfile copies files by name; agent/tools/**.md is deliberately not excluded because that tree is copied wholesale and a skipped deploy would leave the running service stale. test_the_deploy_trigger_covers_everything_the_image_ships reads the Dockerfile's COPY sources and asserts each still triggers a deploy.

nodes.label: 1.24.0 — The commercial roadmap is in the repository now, and that is the smallest change here with the largest effect
nodes.rationale: docs/roadmap.md records the numbering four files referenced without restating the argument (seven items, nine features). Item 3, scheduled delivery, is started, and nearly became the first feature to send issue text out of the tenant through a third-party model; Forge LLMs (@forge/llm, GA July 2026) writes the brief inside the tenant instead, ADR 0013, with projecting issues before prompting rejected. The file still crosses (mail). The guard is a rule: the model never writes a number; template slots are filled in code (ADR 0005), checking numerals afterwards was rejected as judgement-dependent, refused sections are printed verbatim and the model's output discarded using forecast.Refusal.sentence() piped through the JavaScript, a missing figure returns no half-rendered text, a measured zero is a figure (ADR 0010), one unusable section stops the brief, UNCHECKED names what the finite word list cannot catch, and matching is whole-word. Nothing deployed; the weekly-brief trigger has no handler; recipient configuration is the same open question as an ask on Forge.

nodes.label: 1.23.1 — A real Atlassian token has been through the verifier, and it was accepted
nodes.rationale: App 4.0.0 on a dev site: /v1/slice answered 200 with 0 issues in 126 ms (a JWKS miss) and /v1/forecast-context 200 in 4 ms (cache hit), attributed to the installation ARI, with the nested app.installationId claim read correctly, 1.19.0's fault shown fixed in production. This closes the last of docs/forge-deployment.md section 2's conditions. The 4 ms proves the refusal path (ADR 0007), not a figure: the pipe is proved and a forecast travelling it is not.

nodes.label: 1.23.0 — The forecast is wired to the hosted calculator, and remotes[0].baseUrl names a real deployment for the first time
nodes.rationale: Region-pinned europe-west3 and us-central1, chosen by Forge per installation; forge lint reports one MAJOR_VERSION_RULE for the baseUrl format. The resolver asks /v1/slice which contexts to sample rather than assuming the board is the team, because team_slice has been wrong twice with plausible dates; three assertions hold it (the route names the contexts the forecast counts, the resolver has no team comparison, contextId is stamped on every issue because issueFrom does not and selection.forecast_for drops untagged issues). Sequencing refuses with the true reason: a Jira site has nowhere to record an ask. No real token yet; deploying needs --approve MAJOR_VERSION_RULE and a reinstall.

nodes.label: 1.22.0 — The slice moved to where both callers can reach it, and that is the whole change
nodes.rationale: team_slice and forecast_for lived in scripts/serve_live.py, which the Dockerfile does not ship, and the alternative was a second implementation in JavaScript of the code whose failures are all plausible dates (1.8.0's 19 to 77, 1.16.13's 2.5x and 0%-by-today). They are agent/tools/selection.py, a fifth tool module and the first that is not a calculation; serve_live.py imports them. POST /v1/forecast-context takes contexts, issues and a context id and lets the tool choose; /v1/forecast is unchanged; the service still computes nothing, held to selection.forecast_for byte for byte. It refuses on no contexts, 404s an unknown id, and refuses out-of-range items. Context names cross as customer strings, stated. Not yet wired to Forge.

nodes.label: 1.21.0 — The calculator is tenant-aware in production
nodes.rationale: Both regions run SERVICE_AUTH=forge-token with all four Atlassian values and no secret mounted. Atlassian's JWKS fetched live serves six RS256 keys with forge/invocation-token/ key ids, supporting the URL, issuer and algorithm pin. Eight hand-made tokens were refused against the real key set, including an RS256 token with a real kid signed by a key Atlassian never issued; six refusals took 0 ms (algorithm pinned before any key lookup), one 164 ms (live fetch), one 7 ms (cache), with no traceback. The auth mode is chosen by whether FORGE_AUDIENCE is set, so rollback is a variable. Acceptance of a genuine token is still untested; baseUrl still .invalid.

nodes.label: 1.20.3 — The cold start is measured rather than feared
nodes.rationale: 1.15 s in us-central1 and 0.39 s in europe-west3 for a full /v1/forecast on freshly created revisions, against a 25-second token budget, so min-instances stays 0 rather than $9.86 a month per region; limits stated. The shared secret is on version 2 (without the trailing newline) and version 1 is disabled rather than destroyed, with both regions cold-started to prove nothing resolves it.

nodes.label: 1.20.2 — The calculator is hosted
nodes.rationale: us-central1 and europe-west3, scale-to-zero, both refusing unauthenticated callers and issue text; each region's forecast is byte-identical to forecast.build() called directly (5,825 bytes, three machines). _verify_shared_secret stripped the presented token and not the configured one, so any secret store appending a newline (provision-gcp.sh piped openssl rand into Secret Manager) produced a 401 to the correct credential with nothing an operator could see. The wizard pipes through tr -d and _expected_secret() strips; a whitespace-only value is still no value. Four assertions pin it, reverting the strip fails all four.

nodes.label: 1.20.1 — The calculator is deployed and serving in us-central1, and the first deploy reported it as dead
nodes.rationale: Google's front end intercepts the literal path /healthz on Cloud Run and answers its own 404; every other signal was green, and the container's own access log settled it. The probe is /v1/meta expecting 401, which also proves authentication is on. Product routes are unaffected. europe-west3 was left undeployed because the loop aborts on a failed region.

nodes.label: 1.20.0 — The calculator has somewhere to be deployed from, and nothing on the way there holds a key
nodes.rationale: service/provision-gcp.sh is an eight-stage wizard for the half only a person can do and .github/workflows/deploy.yml the half that must never be done by hand. Workload Identity Federation pinned to one repository rather than a service-account key; two service accounts (deployer and runtime) with narrow grants. Container checks moved into service/smoke.sh and the scan policy into service/scan.sh so the weekly rebuild clears the same bar, and the rebuild deploys. --concurrency=1 because CPU-bound CPython under the GIL would push eight concurrent intake.sequence calls past the 25-second token; --timeout=30s. Google auth actions on v3. The deploy skips rather than fails when unprovisioned. Still shared-secret and .invalid so hosting is proved before the Forge wiring.

nodes.label: 1.19.0 — The hosted calculator has a plan, and writing it found that forge-token was never blocked only on four values
nodes.rationale: docs/hosting-the-calculator.md recommends Cloud Run in two regions, request billing, no minimum instances, SERVICE_AUTH=forge-token, and costs three tiers.
