ADR 0012: callCalculator() used plain fetch against process.env.CALCULATOR_URL and would have sent no invocation token; it calls invokeRemote('calculator') with operations: [compute] declared, permissions.external.fetch gone, and the literal key held against the manifest; a manifest-resolved baseUrl is per-install residency. _verify_forge_token() read a flat tenant claim, but the real one is nested app.installationId, so all twelve rejection cases passed against a verifier that could not read a real token; _claim_at() walks a dotted path and a case is minted in Atlassian's published shape. FORGE_LEEWAY_SECONDS at 30 exceeds the 25-second token life and stays until measured. Four values confirmed 2026-08-25; app-system and app-user headers declined. Weekly rebuild deploys; fixable HIGH and CRITICAL block, unfixable print; costed at $0.15 to $3.70 a month.

nodes.label: 1.18.1 — The token verifier raised where it should have refused, and CI found it on the first push
nodes.rationale: _verify_forge_token() imported PyJWT inside the function and threw on a runner that had never installed it, answering the must-not-pass assertion with an exception. The contract is a principal or None, so the import is caught and the function refuses; the startup guard names the missing dependency. Pinned by making import jwt fail on purpose; CI installs service/requirements.txt before the calculator tests.

nodes.label: 1.18.0 — The calculator can authenticate a tenant
nodes.rationale: SERVICE_AUTH=forge-token is written: the verifier returns who the caller is and the tenant reaches the access log (shared-secret mode logs none). Found while checking: callCalculator() sends no Authorization header while the only implemented mode wanted a bearer secret, so the halves had never met. Four values (FORGE_JWKS_URL, FORGE_ISSUER, FORGE_AUDIENCE, FORGE_TENANT_CLAIM) are configuration, refused at startup and per request. Mechanics proved against a suite-controlled signer with twelve forgery cases including alg: none and HMAC-with-the-public-key; two JWKS cache properties pinned. Two mutation tests were worthless on a second look. PyJWT[crypto] in a new service/requirements.txt, not the fetcher's. No real token yet; baseUrl .invalid.

nodes.label: 1.17.1 — Sizing an ask could never work over the route Forge would use, and the reason was one field reaching nobody
nodes.rationale: intake.py grouped finished epics by the epic's summary, which clean_dataset() strips as free text, so over the calculator route epic_sizes() was empty and both sizing methods refused for every board, accurately. epicKey travelled through the resolver, CALC_FIELDS and the allow-list and nobody read it. Sizing keys on epicKey when a dataset carries one, chosen once for the whole issue set because a per-issue fallback would split a single epic into two, a plausible wrong number; the basis line says which. /v1/ask is exercised end to end with free text stripped. 1.16.10's loose-end assertion is retired.

nodes.label: 1.17.0 — Four flow tiles, and none of them needed a sprint or a window
nodes.rationale: Cycle time against 50/85/95 percentile lines, ageing work in progress, weekly throughput with quiet weeks included, and a three-band cumulative flow whose limitation is printed; Little's Law reconciled with no verdict drawn. Shown by default on a flow board and available everywhere, with presets gaining a board-kind column rather than a fourth preset. Every figure is computed in agent/tools/metrics.py first and the page mirrors the percentile function, held to the facts pack by tests/e2e.py. A mutation test on the percentile constant passed because 85 and 80 coincided on the sample data and the caption was a literal; the sentence is built from the constants. The tiles were invisible to tests/a11y.py and are shown explicitly. Left out: blocked time, type distribution (ADR 0004), WIP limits, a flow-efficiency trend, per-person cuts (ADR 0003).

nodes.label: 1.16.13 — The Monte Carlo tile was forecasting a board with no sprints two and a half times too fast
nodes.rationale: team_slice() held each flow-board issue three times across its 14, 30 and 90-day windows, so throughput_samples() counted three completions per finished item and the 85th percentile came back at four working days against a true ten; issues are de-duplicated by key, with a strong-form test that one window and three forecast identically. A window's endDate (today) was passed as the default target, answering 0%; a window now supplies no target and the capacity refusal says 'no end date to forecast against'. Neither was reachable in a tenant (ADR 0008's refusal). next_commitment already refused correctly per 1.16.4.

nodes.label: 1.16.12 — A board with no sprints gets a health score of its own
nodes.rationale: Flow health is built on flow efficiency at 40% with blockers and ageing work at 30% each, the one place a figure is replaced rather than refused. Three components, because there is no honest fourth. Both scores share one machine (drop-and-name, re-weighting, floor, bands). Flow efficiency is load-bearing: without it 60% of the weight survives the floor but what remains is hygiene, so the score refuses and names started as missing. The chip says which composite it carries. One 40% threshold replaces the executive card's 40 and the risk register's 45.

nodes.label: 1.16.11 — A board with no sprints shows the tiles that measure it, and not the three that never can
nodes.rationale: The burndown, commitment history and team load refused in place; the line is whether the condition can lift, and on a flow board it never will, so three permanent apologies become furniture. They are hidden and the sprint-health chip emptied and hidden, corrected in ADR 0011. Nothing is dropped without being named twice: the context bar says why, and the tile picker lists and disables them with reasons, counted separately from tiles the reader turned off. S.shown is masked, never edited. Not a kanban preset, because board kind and audience are different axes. Three 1.16.8 sentences are removed.

nodes.label: 1.16.10 — Cycle time works inside a Jira tenant
nodes.rationale: The resolver never sent started because recognising an in-progress transition needs organisation config. It now sends statusTransitions, every move with its date and the names undecided, and the page picks the earliest one its own config calls in-progress; the rule keeps one implementation. Earliest, not first: Jira's changelog is not date-ordered, and list order moved every start three days later on the demo data, shortening cycle times, so the fixtures are deliberately out of order and e2e fails on the sort alone. The list is uncapped. epicKey reaches no consumer, since intake.py groups by the free-text epic name; it is named and asserted rather than dropped, and every allow-list exception is checked as genuinely referenced.

nodes.label: 1.16.9 — The risk register was reporting a clean bill of health over rules it never ran
nodes.rationale: Three of eight rules depend on something beyond the issues on screen and vanish silently when the condition is false, so 'No risks triggered' stood over a shorter examination than the reader thought. They are named as not run with reasons, and the no-risk sentence becomes 'by the rules that could be run here'. The executive summary names the pace and scope sentences it withheld. Two sprint-shaped register sentences are fixed. tests/e2e.py asserts both directions.

nodes.label: 1.16.8 — Every tile that would have stated a sprint-shaped figure on a flow board now says what it in particular cannot show
nodes.rationale: Step 4, and not a banner over the grid (ADR 0010). Delivered % is withheld because a window's denominator is partly defined by being in the numerator; Scope added is withheld because addedMidSprint has no referent on a board with no sprints, and both figures return the moment the guard is removed. The executive summary states counts and withholds the share. Four tiles named causes that would send a reader to fix the wrong thing; each names the board and ends with the tools' closing clause. 'Likely to carry over' is renamed Still open rather than refused, and the ageing chart stops calling a fortnight a sprint.

nodes.label: 1.16.7 — The page knows a window is not a clock
nodes.rationale: Step 3: contextWorkingDays() withholds a working-day list for a window before the sent list is consulted, and derive() withholds timeElapsed at source because renderExec reads paceGap directly; the mutation printed Pace vs clock -45 pp for a board that committed to nothing. Scope stability read 100/100 on a window from a divide-by-zero guard (the shape ADR 0009 caught the resolver in); both measures are dropped and named, the score refuses at 0.44 of the weight, and the fourth cause gets its own single sentence (ADR 0010). Three overlapping windows must never be rolled up. The picker says Window.

nodes.label: 1.16.6 — A board that runs no sprints is offered something for the first time
nodes.rationale: Three windows (14, 30 and 90 days) are offered and loaded together over both transports. The resolver fetches through /board/{id}/issue; the loopback goes through the board's saved filter via jira_pull(); the membership predicate is one pure function mirrored in both languages on resolutiondate, with an upper bound of the day after the window because Jira compares a bare date against midnight, pinned by a test that fails on the operator alone. The footer's one count became two sentences and moved into forge/src/jira.js. The window's length is in the id and its dates are resolved at load. A window still carries no working-day list. ADR 0009 is corrected: the app now issues some JQL, but only three date pairs per board from a canonical token parseContextId refuses anything else for.

nodes.label: 1.16.5 — The two transports now agree what a window is, before either one offers a board a window
nodes.rationale: Step 1: a flow board's id is SFT/2/win:30d and kind ('sprint' or 'window') is carried rather than re-derived (ADR 0011), with BundleBackend defaulting to sprint. A value-level parity check builds the same window in both languages across month ends, a year end and a leap year, because the existing field-set check is the hole workingDays went missing through. win:030d parsed as the same context as win:30d; a token is checked by rebuilding it so only the canonical spelling parses. Lengths outside 14, 30 and 90 are refused.

nodes.label: 1.16.4 — A dataset that stated no sprint dates was told how many items to commit to
nodes.rationale: forecast.build() read the working-day count with a trailing 'or 10', substituting a ten-day sprint before recommend_commitment()'s 'sprint length is unknown' refusal could fire, so a file with no calendar got 'commit to 9 items' with a stated basis. The fallback is gone; reaching for orgConfig.sprintLengthDays was rejected as the same bug because from_dataset() merges defaults. tests/test_agent.py pins both directions. ADR 0011 decides what a board with no sprints is offered: a window bounding the selection with no working-day list, a second caller of ADR 0010's drop-and-name rule; sprint health and Delivered % refuse on it, the KPI strip does not go as one. CONTEXT.md takes the vocabulary and docs/kanban-boards.md names every tile's fate.

nodes.label: 1.16.2 — Reconciled with the per-site calendar work, which landed on main in parallel
nodes.rationale: The resolver sends the site's config and the page derives the day list; the resolver still must not compute working days, because that rule has two tested implementations already. The e2e parity check now feeds a body shaped as the resolver shapes one, with workingDays, statusCategory and contextId stripped. A missing calendar scored Delivery pace 0/100 at 34% weight, turning the sample sprint from Amber to Red: an unmeasured component is now dropped, named and the rest re-weighted; below half the weight the score refuses; a points view over an unestimated dataset had broken two measures in opposite directions. 'No sprint calendar' was printed for three causes; there are three sentences. The chip reads '(33/100, 3 of 4 measures)' and printed weights sum to 100. ADR 0010 carries both halves.

nodes.label: 1.16.1 — The dashboard scored an empty sprint 66 out of 100
nodes.rationale: Over a dataset with no issues the divide-by-zero guards (Math.max(items.length, 1), ? ... : 0) all resolve to good news and the four weights summed to a figure that looks computed. That is the state the Forge build opens in, since the seed carries no issues, and a search matching nothing reaches it too. Zero issues is a refusal across the executive card, KPI strip, ageing chart, value card, risk register and health score, in the tools' words with the closing clause; counts of an empty set that are honestly nil keep their nil (ADR 0010). The grid is no longer faded, and tests/a11y.py renders the empty state in both themes. tests/e2e.py sweeps six elements for digits and asserts the score returns when there are issues.

nodes.label: 1.16.0 — The dashboard inside Forge shows the customer's own Jira, not a demo company's
nodes.rationale: ADR 0009: one contract, two transports. The page asks four questions by route name and gets {ok, status, body}; bodies are defined by serve_live.py and returned unchanged by the resolvers; src/app.js knows nothing of Forge and the adapter forge/bridge/bridge.js is a classic script ahead of app.js, CommonJS inside a try because @forge/bridge throws outside a frame (found by loading the real bundle). The first real install came up blank: sprintsFor swallowed a 403 as 'no sprints', a rejected invoke() was treated as a dead loopback, and two Jira endpoints disagreed about board.location so every sprint was an unknown context; the id now uses Forge's module context. 'Server returned 404' becomes four sentences. forge/src/jira.js is pure and compared against serve_live envelopes in test_service; e2e compares rendering over both. addedMidSprint is read from the changelog because defaulting false is a claim; statusCategory, started and the burndown are deliberately not sent. The Forge build is seeded empty. Three scopes. The scaffold check becomes a baseUrl/refusal biconditional. A tenant is measured under its own calendar: done statuses from Jira's own categories, the rest from an orgConfig project property, validated in JavaScript against orgconfig.validate over nineteen fixtures; story points discovered by display name via /rest/api/3/field; null never 0.

nodes.label: 1.15.1 — The three things the Forge work left unfinished now have runbooks
nodes.rationale: docs/forge-deployment.md is the guide. SERVICE_AUTH selects shared-secret or forge-token, and the unwritten mode refuses to start and refuses every request rather than degrading; what the verifier must check and eleven forgery cases are written down instead of guessed. The manifest is checked on every push: scopes match SCOPES in jira_auth.py, the egress rule names a declared remote, no write or manage scope, no app id committed. The container image is built and smoke-tested in CI, and test_service reconstructs the image's filesystem from the Dockerfile's COPY lines and imports the service from it. The security suite flagged a literal secret in the CI job, minted per run now.

nodes.label: 1.15.0 — If we ship on Forge, the forecast comes with us
nodes.rationale: ADR 0008: Forge runs Node and cannot execute agent/tools/, so the Python is hosted as a calculator rather than rewritten. The tools were already pure functions; service/app.py is a second caller after serve_live.py. A call is 16 KB regardless of customer size. No issue title has to leave: forecast.build() over a dataset stripped to ten fields is byte-identical, and summary and assignee are re-attached by key in the Forge app; free text is refused with 400 at both ends and the field lists are compared across languages. The service computes nothing, proved byte for byte against forecast.build(). It refuses to start without a shared secret; refusals survive the trip with the calendar named. The security suite caught a literal bearer token in the tests. Forge itself has never run. Costs written down: the Runs on Atlassian badge forfeited, residency ours, a service to operate.

nodes.label: 1.14.0 — Phase 1 of the commercial roadmap: make it connectable
nodes.rationale: Jira connects over OAuth 2.0 (3LO) in scripts/jira_auth.py; --auth auto prints which credential it used; a grant covering two sites is refused; scopes are read:jira-work and read:jira-user with a test failing on any write scope. Which statuses mean done, the working week, holidays and sprint length are config/organisation.json resolved by agent/tools/orgconfig.py and written into the dataset as orgConfig; the page, metrics.py, forecast.py, intake.py and the live server read it from there and none opens the file, because a separately read config is a third opinion (the 25%/22% shape). Unseen statuses are named; a bad config stops the run; holidays shorten working time only. Bug found: forecast.py honoured meta.workingDays in one place and built its own Monday-to-Friday span in five others. Defaults change no number. src/app.js mirrors orgconfig.py and tests/e2e.py compares them under a non-default config. The footer says which calendar. The security suite re-covers the credential path with six checks. forge/ is a scaffold and marked as one.

nodes.label: 1.13.0 — The tiles can be put in your own order
nodes.rationale: Up and down arrows per row rather than drag and drop, because dragging is unusable from a keyboard and the page is held to WCAG 2.2 AA. The order travels as ?order= and data-order, never browser storage. applyOrder() re-appends the nodes rather than setting CSS order, which would leave the reading order behind; e2e compares DOM order on every move. Focus survives the move and a live region announces it. Order and selection stay independent. A custom order may leave a row short and is labelled as custom. An unreadable ?order= degrades to the whole page in an odd sequence. The popover is measured open at 320px.

nodes.label: 1.12.5 — Two rows of the tile grid did not add up to 12, and the page had the holes to prove it
nodes.rationale: Release quality at 4 beside Team load at 3 left roughly 600x360px empty; both are 6 now. Between 761 and 1180px the breakpoint promoted wide tiles to full width and orphaned their partners; it halves everything instead, 4557px of page becoming 3848px. Cards stretch to their row. tests/e2e.py sums the column span of every visible tile per row at three widths and requires 12; its first version read grid-column-end, which computes to auto, so every row summed to 24 and could never have passed.

nodes.label: 1.12.4 — The theme button lied on a machine that prefers dark
nodes.rationale: The prefers-color-scheme branch set the attribute directly instead of going through setTheme(), so a dark-preferring machine opened dark under a button reading Dark, which is also the control's accessible name. The branch sets the label alongside the attribute; the accessibility suite opens a page under an emulated dark preference and asserts the pair.

nodes.label: 1.12.3 — The demo now shows the Monte Carlo tile, all three questions
nodes.rationale: Four new scenes. Recording required serving the page: record_demo.py starts serve_live.py against the demo bundle and drives the page over http, serving the same bundle the page displays so no disagreement is put on film. The recorder can type into a field and wait for a fetch. Both cuts re-recorded.

nodes.label: 1.12.2 — The 320px reflow failure was a sparkline, not the tile
nodes.rationale: The value card's fixed 110px sparkline in a non-wrapping flex row overflowed to 324px on a 320px screen, its endpoint marker painting outside the SVG. The row wraps, the chart never exceeds its column, and spark() insets both axes by the marker radius. The reflow check now names the offending elements with their right edges, which is how CI identified it.

nodes.label: 1.12.1 — Fixed a WCAG 1.4.10 reflow failure introduced by the third forecast mode
nodes.rationale: A Sequence asks button made the segmented control 260px wide under flex-wrap: nowrap; on CI's Linux font metrics the page needed 399px. Card headers, tool groups and the control all wrap, and below 760px the tools take their own row. The suite was checking 380px where WCAG specifies 320; it checks both and asserts no control comes within 8px of the 320px edge.

nodes.label: 1.12.0 — Ask sequencing is on the tile
nodes.rationale: A third forecast mode runs intake.sequence() for the selected board over data/asks/. It leads with asks that miss their date in every ordering, names asks it could not size with the tool's reason, and still returns no value score, printing the tool's closing sentence verbatim. A board with no asks says so; a live Jira connection declines with a reason rather than assembling a partial dataset; the tile no longer claims to print the same output as make intake-sequence, which defaults to a different bundle.

nodes.label: 1.11.0 — The forecast tile takes an input, so it answers hypotheticals as well as the sprint in front of you
nodes.rationale: When accepts an item count and How many a date, both defaulting to the selected sprint's figures; an asked-for figure is labelled as one and rejected input is refused with 400 and explained rather than silently reverted. A bug this would have shipped: each trial was abandoned after 400 working days silently, so a request beyond the team's pace returned every percentile at exactly 400. forecast_completion() counts abandoned trials, returns unfinished_fraction and names the horizon in its basis line; the tile prints 'These dates are a floor'. The no-silent-caps rule applied to the forecaster.

nodes.label: 1.10.0 — The Monte Carlo forecast is on the dashboard, not just in a terminal
nodes.rationale: A tile calls agent/tools/forecast.py through api/forecast in serve_live.py; nothing in the page computes a forecast, and the tile shows an offline notice in an emailed file. It samples the team's whole history (55 observations against 2 for one sprint), sliced by team and falling back to project and board, with only the outstanding count from the selected sprint; conflating those is the 1.8.0 bug, and a test pins both halves. build() samples every recorded day rather than a 90-day tail, byte-identical on every dataset in the repo today and asserted so. size_stability() reports drift. serve_live.py now imports forecast.py, the first scripts-to-tools dependency.

nodes.label: 1.9.2 — The source badge denied live connections that were working
nodes.rationale: The badge read meta.sourceLabel, what the loaded dataset says about itself, and never consulted S.live, so the bundled demo's 'Demo data (no live connection)' printed while a server served eighteen sprints. It reports the connection when there is one and the dataset's label otherwise, with the tooltip stating both. Pinned in tests/security.py, the only suite holding a browser and a server, confirmed by reverting.

nodes.label: 1.9.1 — The live-mode server dropped the connection on any 404 instead of sending it
nodes.rationale: log_message() tested '/api/' in a[0], and log_error passes an HTTPStatus, so membership raised after the 404 was decided and before it was written; a favicon request fired it on every page load. Worse, three path-traversal checks passed because of it, asserting only that a body lacked root: and a dropped connection has no body. They now require a real 403 or 404, and a fourth asserts a plain missing file gets a clean 404. All four fail against the unfixed server.

nodes.label: 1.9.0 — Tiles can be turned off, so one file can be sent to two audiences
nodes.rationale: A Tiles button with Executive and Team presets shaped after agent/templates/exec-brief.md and team-report.md, pinned together by a test. Visibility changes nothing counted: every figure comes from the same derive() and a test asserts headline numbers are byte-identical with tiles hidden. A saved view carries the loaded data rather than the seed, because after an upload the dataset lives in memory; the test saves and reopens a 242-issue bundle. The view travels baked into a copy, in print, and in the URL, never browser storage. Hidden tiles are named. An unrecognised ?tiles= shows everything.

nodes.label: 1.8.2 — PUSH.md and scripts/setup-on-mac.sh are gone
nodes.rationale: Both existed for a one-time transition that has happened. PUSH.md mostly restated README.md and had drifted from it; the README now carries the corrected Pages statement, including that the job publishes the whole of data/. A document for a one-time transition should be deleted when the transition completes.

nodes.label: 1.8.1 — The Pages workflow is manual-only now
nodes.rationale: It triggered on every push and copies the whole of data/ into a public site, which holds real issue titles once the fetcher has run; nothing leaked only because Pages was not enabled. The trigger is workflow_dispatch only, so publishing is a deliberate act, and a permanent red cross on every push goes with it. PUSH.md's claim that it was not enabled by default is corrected.

nodes.label: 1.8.0 — Product intake
nodes.rationale: agent/tools/intake.py forecasts an ask before a ticket exists: a described request plus a team in, a sized range with two delivery scenarios and attributed uncertainty out. Sizing is a ladder with the rung declared: tshirt bands cut from the board's own completed epics (refusing below eight), reference-class, and explicit, each with its caveat verbatim. Two capacity scenarios always, with the queue's cost in working days. Uncertainty is split between size and delivery variability. A readiness gate runs first. Sequencing returns consequences, never a score (no WSJF). Three scope bugs returned plausible wrong numbers: board_issues() returned the first context rather than the most recent (a 16-item ask at 77 working days instead of 19), the interruption rate came from whichever context was last in the file, and queue_ahead() ignored its as_of; pinned by an intake scope section in tests/test_agent.py. The CLI printed four readiness gaps while counting all. docs/product-intake.md, a template, three asks and a separate intake bundle added.

nodes.label: 1.7.0 — Overtime removed
nodes.rationale: The organisation does not operate overtime, and charting hours implied a time-tracking regime that does not exist; both series of Sustainable pace went, because output per person alone is the individual-performance framing this dashboard refuses. The card is Team load: work in progress and unplanned work, from issue status only. overtimeHrs and teamPutsSP are gone everywhere. The accessibility suite (make test-a11y) found 67 low-contrast nodes, fixed with separate UI tokens (--link, --accent-bg, --info-ink) so the chart palette stays validated; white glyphs on warning yellow at 1.8:1; focus lost on closing the drill-down; a source chip styled as a status. The security suite found a real stored XSS (issue keys and summaries interpolated unescaped), fixed with a single esc() at output plus safeUrl(), and covers injection, prototype pollution, no network, no persistence, path traversal, XXE and zip-slip, secrets and dependencies. make_sample_bundle.py emitted empty burndowns.

nodes.label: 1.6.0 — A shareable demo, and an executive summary of the agent
nodes.rationale: docs/demo.mp4 is a captioned, silent walkthrough recorded from the real built file by scripts/record_demo.py so it cannot drift; docs/agent-executive-summary.md addresses leadership; scripts/make_demo_bundle.py is authored to tell a story across three boards; the closing forecast figures come from the real forecaster; two encodes; make demo rebuilds both.

nodes.label: 1.5.1 — Performance measured rather than assumed
nodes.rationale: tests/perf.py instruments a real browser at four bundle sizes: interaction cost is flat in dataset size because only the selected sprint is drawn, building the sprint dropdown costs 0.2 ms either way, and the ceiling is payload (2.8 MB, 79% issues) where stripping saves 8%. No optimisation was made because none was warranted; the harness is committed. make bundle --scale N clones the demo board set.

nodes.label: 1.5.0 — Project, board and sprint filtering
nodes.rationale: schemaVersion 2.0 bundles carry contexts[] and a contextId per issue with per-context burndown, history, releases and DORA; v1.0 files load unchanged. Cascading pickers, an All N sprints rollup whose burndown and release cards explain why they do not apply, and each context's history holding only sprints up to itself. The fetcher builds bundles with --jira-boards. Optional live mode: scripts/serve_live.py exposes api/contexts and api/context, the page probes and merges stubs, skipped on file://. Fixed: normalise() re-tagged live issues with the wrong context id.

nodes.label: 1.4.0 — The dashboard now measures in items by default, with a Points toggle
nodes.rationale: Closes the last place the dashboard and the agent reported the same sprint in different units. A Measure control switches the burndown, four tiles, the distribution and commitment history; burndown[] and history[] carry item series computed in the browser import, the fetcher and scripts/rebuild_burndown.py, pinned to one answer. Table views show both units. Health, narrative and risks follow the unit and the tooltip states it. Old datasets render in points and say why. The sample burndown was rebuilt from its own issues after claiming 47 points where the issues said 42.

nodes.label: 1.3.0 — Item counts made the unit end to end
nodes.rationale: The forecaster never used points but the recommendation layer did. recommend_commitment() runs a Monte Carlo over a simulated sprint returning items at each confidence and recommends the 85% figure; size_stability() detects a team splitting work smaller (drift and spread); metrics.py predictability is item-primary with points marked as not a forecasting input; the agent definition and templates size commitments in items.

nodes.label: 1.2.0 — Reporting and forecasting agent (agent/)
nodes.rationale: Design in docs/forecasting-agent.md, definition in agent/SKILL.md. A hard split between deterministic reporting and probabilistic forecasting; the agent narrates and never computes, every figure from metrics.py or forecast.py. Monte Carlo over item throughput, 20,000 seeded trials; refuses below documented thresholds with verbatim text; scope growth sampled where available; ageing on two clocks; change detection; Brier calibration; a walk-forward backtest with non-overlapping windows. Fixes found by the new tests: the facts pack and dashboard disagreed on flow efficiency (25% vs 22%) from mixing calendar and working days, so units are declared on every block; twelve weeks of history counted as sprint scope; an earlier backtest's 38% coverage came from overlapping windows.

nodes.label: 1.1.0 — Upload pipeline
nodes.rationale: Replaces a strict-schema import that failed on any real export: csv, tsv, xlsx (parsed natively via DecompressionStream) and json including raw Jira and Asana exports; column auto-matching with an override step; date handling that flags undecidable day-first versus month-first rather than guessing; mid-sprint additions inferred from the sprint start; merge mode; a preview with warnings; burndown and the current history row recalculated from uploaded issues. The repository splits into src, data, scripts, docs, tests and dist with a dependency-free build.py, a Makefile, CI failing on a stale dist, an optional Pages workflow and an end-to-end browser suite. Small layout fixes.

nodes.label: 1.0.0 — First version
nodes.rationale: Single-file dashboard with cross-filtering, drill-downs on every element, table views, a computed risk register, a health score with disclosed method, dark mode, print layout, CSV export, and the Jira/Asana fetcher script.
